text:
Maria: quick update from the nova11b bring-up slice runs — ran the GTN slice suite + 3 product slices (long-rewrite, short-qa, instruction-follow). high-level: int6 saves a lot but has quality hit on long-rewrite.

Ajay: numbers?

Maria: sure — median tokens/request = 110, p95 latency int8=220ms int6=240ms, cost delta ~= -42% per token for int6 vs int8. human acceptance (GTN blind eval): int8=94.1% vs int6=90.7% (delta -3.4ppt). sample n=600 per slice.

Sophie: ok that delta is non-trivial for GTN where correctness matters. any slice breakdown?

Maria: yes — short-qa negligible (-0.6ppt), instruction-follow -1.2ppt, long-rewrite -7.8ppt. long-rewrite errors are style/fluency drops, occasional hallucination on edge facts.

Ben: do we have statistical significance?

Maria: short-qa p=0.12, instruction-follow p=0.03, long-rewrite p<0.001. so long-rewrite is clearly regressing.

Sophie: proposal: route deterministic / high-precision slices to int6 with a strict per-slice delta guard; keep creative/long-rewrite on int8. default fallback to int8.

Ajay: what thresholds? product needs a simple rule to hand to GTN.

Maria: suggested thresholds (for GTN rollout):
- allowed overall human-accept delta <= 1.0ppt
- per-slice delta threshold = 1.5ppt (if any slice >1.5ppt rollback)
- p-value < 0.05 required for slice-level action

Sophie: sounds reasonable. also add a metric for downstream regressions: reduction in rated helpfulness or increase in clarification prompts. those should be in the gating signal.

Maria: agreed. here's a quick routing flag snippet we tested (dev-config):
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"name":"deterministic","match":"structured_prompt","model":"nova11b-int6","pct":40},
    {"name":"creative","match":"open_generation","model":"nova11b-int8","pct":60}
  ],
  "fallback": "nova11b-int8",
  "observability": {"sample_rate": 0.02, "slice_checks": ["long-rewrite","short-qa","instruction-follow"]}
}
```

Ben: how confident are we on unit-econ numbers? need to present to GTN finance.

Maria: cost per 1M tokens (approx): int8 = $1400, int6 = $820. these are infra-only numbers (GPU + infra amortized). with caching and prefix reuse we expect marginal token cost to be lower for both but delta remains ~40%.

Ajay: any mitigations to reduce int6 quality gap? distillation / small-temp tuning?

Maria: tried small LR finetune on 200k supervised examples for long-rewrite slice — acceptance improved from 90.7% -> 92.9% (delta vs int8 now -1.2ppt) but introduces maintenance and regen debt. also increases model size on storage pipeline marginally (new checkpoints).

Sophie: tradeoffs noted. GTN likely accepts up to ~1ppt overall if cost savings >30%, but they want per-slice guard. so the finetune path is attractive as a compromise if we can automate retrain in the onboarding pipeline.

ops-bot: deploy-check: canary traffic configured (40% int6 on structured routes) — monitoring hooks active for human-accept and p95 latency. alerts: slice-delta > 1.5ppt or p95 regressed > 20% -> page eng-ml oncall.

Maria: action items:
- (Maria) run extended long-rewrite finetune + n=2k eval by EOD Thu
- (Sophie) draft GTN playbook paragraph with thresholds and fallback language
- (Ajay) cost appendix with infra and projected savings (include amortized retrain costs)
- (Ben) validate metric hooks and ops-bot alert thresholds

Ajay: timeline for GTN handoff?

Sophie: if finetune looks good and cost appendix approved, propose staged rollout next Tue: 0->10->30->60% with slice checks at each step.

Ben: noted. I'll also add an A/B for user-facing retention metric (7-day engagement) to catch any latent quality drift.

Maria: thanks all — will post eval artifacts (csv + raw rater comments) in the onboarding folder once the extended run finishes. :thumbsup:
